Getting started › Your first static site

Your first static site

You will turn a few TypeScript files into JavaScript with the pare command and open them in a browser. No .NET project, no Node, no bundler.

1. Install pare

Download pare-<version>-<rid>.tar.gz for your system from the releases page (.zip on Windows), unpack it and put the folder on your PATH:

bash 
tar -xzf pare-0.6.1-osx-arm64.tar.gz
export PATH="$PWD/pare-0.6.1-osx-arm64:$PATH"
pare --version

The Extrode.Pare.Cli .NET tool package is not on nuget.org yet, so the archive is the way in.

2. Get the sample

The repository has a ready-made page in samples/CliSite: three TypeScript modules in src/. main.ts imports the other two and uses interfaces, generics, satisfies, as, ! and a type-only import.

bash 
git clone https://github.com/extrode/pare
cd pare

3. Strip it

bash 
pare samples/CliSite/src --outdir samples/CliSite/js

4. Serve it

Any static server works:

bash 
python3 -m http.server 8000 -d samples/CliSite

Open http://localhost:8000. You should see "2 of 3 open" over three tasks sorted by priority, and "Add task" adds one. Before you ran pare, the page said "JavaScript did not run".

5. Read the output

Open samples/CliSite/js/main.js next to src/main.ts. The types are spaces, so every line and column matches. The imports changed from ./model.ts to ./model.js, because browsers load the .js files:

js 
import { byPriority, summary,           } from "./model.js";
const list = document.querySelector("#tasks")                    ;

Using it on your own project

bash 
pare src                        # every src/**/*.ts becomes .js next to its source
pare src --outdir dist          # mirror the folder structure into dist/
pare "src/**/*.ts" --check-only # report errors, write nothing
pare --stdin < in.ts > out.js   # one file from stdin to stdout

See The pare command for the rest, including how to re-run it on every save.
